text:
anita: Heads up — perf CI flagged a decode-path regression after merge PR #4221. Short-seq p95 up ~18% (locally and on canary). Should we hold the rollout?

jay: I can reproduce. Locally shortseq workload shows an extra kernel switch during decode at token ~8 which wasn't there before.

li: profiler flame looks like: more memcpy/KV eviction churn in the hotpath. attaching a quick excerpt:
```
flame: decode -> attn_kernel_v2 -> kv_cache->memcpy (+12% samples)
callers: attn_kernel_select -> schedule_batch -> execute_kernel
```

mike: Interesting — PR 4221 changed kernel-scheduler priority weights + batching prefilter. Might be forcing a fallback kernel for short sequences. Also saw more small micro-batches in traces.

perf-bot: Regression detected: job perf/shortseq (main) baseline p95=42.1ms current p95=49.7ms (+18.2%). Trace attached: https://perf.redwood/report/4221/shortseq

ci-bot: perf CI failed on commit abc123 (PR 4221) — see job perf/shortseq. Compare: https://ci.redwood/abc123

sophia: Are we sure this is a kernel selection flip and not kv cache pressure? Both would explain higher memcpy and more kernel switches.

jay: I inspected the kernel-selector logs. When seq_len <= 16 the selector picks kernel X (priority increased) but on some models it triggers additional pre/post transforms that cost more than expected. Selector change looks like the minimal delta.

li: Dump from a failing trace (trimmed):
```
[trace] model=redwood-base seq=12
  -> select_kernel: weight([X:0.9, Y:0.1])
  -> schedule: inserted pre-transform conv_transpose (8us)
  -> exec: kv_evict 3 entries (memcopy 1.2ms)
```

mike: The micro-batcher tweak in the PR also reduces prefix coalescing for shortseqs — more distinct batches means cache warmup lost. That increases KV evictions and memcopies.

anita: Proposal: hold the canary rollout and revert the kernel-scheduler weight change from PR 4221 while we bisect the micro-batcher tweak separately.

sophia: +1. We should also add a shortseq perf test that exercises seq<=16 with small batch fanout to catch this in CI.

jay: I'll prepare a minimal revert PR (revert kernel weight tweak only). If perf returns to baseline we know selector is culprit. If not, next step bisect micro-batcher change.

li: For tracing / bisect tips: enable `--trace-kernel-selector` and `--kv-metrics=verbose` on the canary machines; collect 5 runs. Also capture nvprof SMT wall-time for the candidate kernels.

perf-bot: Recommended rollback window: 30m. Impact: canary p95 delta > 15% for shortseq.

anita: OK locking rollout. @jay you own the revert PR. @mike please prepare a shortseq regression test and add to perf CI; @li help with trace flags and a small reproduction harness. We'll re-run perf CI after the revert.

mike: on it — I'll draft the perf test and link in the revert PR.

jay: creating revert PR now: https://git.redwood/reverts/4221-revert-kernel-weight — will link CI once ready.

ci-bot: Notifying: release pipeline paused for canary channel until manual resume.

anita: Thanks team. We'll reconvene after the revert perf results. :thumbsup:
